newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast light crude rallies, but trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast light crude rallies, but trade quiet.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose sharply with NYMEX, making a normally quiet Monday session, even quieter.
West Coast traders expected to ride out a crude rally, which saw the front-month contract up over $1 at $25.68.
Spot West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the basis for Alaskan crude prices, rose 90 cents from Friday to $25.50/25.60 a barrel.
Highly-priced futures, strong export opportunities, and concerns that renewed Kurdish fighting could impede Iraqi oil sales, prompted perceptions of tight supply for WTI.
This propelled Alaska North Slope (ANS) up 80 cents to $23/23.30 a barrel early.
Traders said a broker offered a 500,000 barrel cargo of Koch Alberta crude to a key California refiner, but the firm turned it down after learning it was only for sale outside the Pacific Northwest.
Buyers bid at $2.50 under November WTI, while a major producer continued to offer at $2.10.
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River crude eased five cents in reaction to last week's futures correction, dipping to 17.15/17.35 a barrel.
Prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude also fell with revised postings to $18.50/18.60 a barrel.
